transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I've been struggling with these uncontrollable repetitive behaviors and rituals that I just can't seem to stop. I find myself constantly washing my hands and checking things over and over, which is taking up a lot of my time and causing me a ton of anxiety.

Do you perform these repetitive behaviors because you have persistent, intrusive, and unwanted thoughts or images that you are trying to neutralize, or is it primarily a general feeling of worry about many different aspects of your daily life?

It is definitely because of those persistent, intrusive thoughts rather than just a general worry about daily life. I get these overwhelming, unwanted thoughts about contamination or some kind of disaster happening if I don't do them. Performing the rituals is the only way I can get temporary relief from that intense anxiety.

latest_inference.note: The patient explicitly confirmed that their repetitive behaviors are driven by persistent, intrusive, and unwanted thoughts (obsessions) rather than generalized worry, which strongly supports a diagnosis of Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder and makes Generalized Anxiety Disorder unlikely. I am confident in this diagnosis.
